title: One line in the book
goals: A trial with its name and its colour.
The book can write it down in one line.
starting_code:
class {familiar_class}(Familiar):
    # In place of `pass`, write `__init__` with `self`, `name` and `color`.
    # Its first line keeps the name in `self`.
    # Its second line keeps the colour in `self`.
    pass

# Make {familiar}, with its name and its colour, in one line.

# Call it with `minka`.
hints: Python runs `__init__` by itself every time an object is born, and gives it that object in `self`.
`__init__` is written with `def`, inside the class, and takes three things: `self`, the name and the colour. Inside, each piece of data is kept in `self` with the dot.
Outside the class, the name and the colour go between the class's brackets, in that order and in quotes.
intro: The book of Arvelia writes each familiar down in a single line, and a description that cannot make it born in one line does not go in. Teach your class to make yours born whole.
outro: Look: Tolu, {friend}'s hare, is stepping out of the circle. It is the first familiar of the class to live.
learned: Now you know that `__init__` is the action a class runs by itself when an object is born, that `self` is the object being born, and that anyone can use your class without reading your program if they know what `__init__` takes.
